text:
Alex K: Quick experiment proposal — fractional queue credits to mitigate long/short tenant starvation on the P100 fleet. Idea: instead of one big reserve for long sequences, give small periodic top-ups so short requests still get served.
Maya R: curious — what's the refill cadence you're thinking? and how does this interact with KV warmup? :thinking_face:
Alex K: thinking about a 25ms refill tick with 2% of a normal token budget each tick. rough config snippet:
```ini
queue.refill_fraction=0.02
queue.refill_ms=25
queue.max_burst_fraction=0.2
``` 
Samir: sketch looks ok. main risk is KV cache churn if we let long seqs run with tiny top-ups; they might evict short-request prefixes more often.
Jess L: ran a 1h perf profile on staging with similar rule. KV hit-rate for short seq dropped ~3.5% at 95th, but end-to-end p95 latency for short requests improved by ~12ms. grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abcd/queue-experiments
Maya R: can we add a guard that pauses refill for tenants that have <20% KV hit? prevents churn for sensitive tenants.
Alex K: good call. propose tenant-level KV-sensitivity flag + pause-refill when KV_hit_last_min < 0.2. fallback: normal behavior for non-sensitive tenants.
Samir: also want to cap consecutive ticks per request to avoid infinite slow-drip. i propose max_ticks=150 (so long seq still bounded).
Jess L: perf regression note — one workload saw generator kernel fallback more often under fractional credits. leads to extra kernel-select overhead. We should monitor kernel-switch-rate metric.
Alex K: ok add kernel.switch_rate and kv.eviction_rate to the smoke dashboard. I'll run a canary on 10% of p100 pods tomorrow morning (06:30 UTC).
infra-bot: Deploy scheduled by Alex K for 2026-03-19 06:30 UTC — canary=10% — config: queue.refill_fraction=0.02, queue.refill_ms=25 — status: pending
Maya R: nice. let's collect traces + token-bucket histograms. if KV hit drops >5% for short-reqs or kernel.switch_rate increases >2x, auto-roll back.
Alex K: agreed. I'll push the rollout plan and add an alert rule for those thresholds. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
